items.how: Thesis: widening said once ('one course keeping all another keeps and letting more form, is exactly what every positive weighting ranks higher (`Weighting.widens_iff_every_positive`): what every way of counting each thing as worth something agrees on, and no second premise'); the hypotheses sentence now 'the continuation condition (...), self-concern, or `Comparison`, the order ranking a course above every course it widens, named C'. Bases: 'where a result ranks courses, the continuation condition, self-concern or `Comparison` (C), as its theorem takes them'. §1 Supplied row: 'for a ranking, the condition, self-concern or C (`Comparison`) as its theorem takes them'. §4 heading now '4. How far concern reaches, and how it ranks courses' (explicit anchors kept: scope-and-order, 4-scope-and-order-two-premises-two-roles, 4-scope-and-order-two-readings-two-roles, and the fifth pass's slug 4-how-scope-and-order-emerge-together-from-continuation). The Name|Role table with scope/order rows is replaced by 'What §4 shows | Where it holds | What it does not do': the condition read on relations and held de se (where it holds; ranks nothing), self-concern = increasing in admission (where), self-concern ranks every widening (finite listing; level paths whose admitted pairs fit a finite list; not courses forming without end), widening = what every positive weighting ranks higher (rank mixed comparisons). Paragraph after: 'Neither the condition nor self-concern stands above becoming ...'; 'Widening is no second premise beside it'; 'C names the order that ranks a course above every course it widens (`Comparison`), and the name is used where a theorem takes `Comparison`'. Closing paragraph: 'There what C asks needs no premise of its own beside the condition: an order holding one's own continuation does it'; 'C is a named order' gone. §4.4 heading 'Widening: what every weighting that counts everything shares' (explicit anchor for the old slug 44-c-what-every-weighting-that-counts-everything-shares); 'it decomposes C ... ranking by it is C. Monotonicity ... is C placed at the standpoint' -> 'what standpoints whose orders increase in admission share is exactly widening, so widening is what every way of counting each thing as worth something agrees on, and C names ranking by it. An order increasing in admission is monotone at its standpoint; where the condition holds de se, self-concern is such an order'; 'what C adds having moved into ranking by widening' -> 'the order C names being, on level paths, ranking by widening'; 'C's content, read in' -> 'what C names'; 'there C is self-concern's monotonicity' -> 'there self-concern is increasing in admission and ranks every widening above, as C asks on that listing'. §2 readings: 'Ranking by widening is still C's' -> 'Widening is what every positive weighting ranks higher'; 'for C,' dropped. §4.7: 'beyond that C is a named order' gone. §5: 'C ranks a course above' -> 'an order meeting C (`Comparison`) ranks'; 'with the condition for scope and C for order' -> 'with the condition and C where a result takes them'. §6/§7 labels: 'the condition for scope; C ... for order' -> 'the continuation condition, an order ranking by widening and the practical commitments'; 'Given scope and order' -> 'Given the continuation condition and an order ranking by widening'; '(the continuation condition for scope, C read as widening for order, ...)' -> '(the continuation condition, C read as widening, J1–J4, correspondence E)'; 'read under scope and order' -> 'read under them'; 'the order is C's and J's' -> 'the moves are ranked by widening and by J1/J2'; both 'under C, with the continuation condition for scope' in the revision readings -> 'one ranking by widening, every continuation counted'. T5: 'That valuers value positively is C's premise relocated' -> 'That actual valuers count every item above zero is what the thesis takes, not shown'. T8: 'under C or another named order' -> 'a result that ranks courses states the order its theorem takes, and what every positive weighting agrees on is widening'. §9: 'C leaves gross partiality' -> 'widening leaves'; 'which losses C counts' -> 'which losses count'; 'priority agrees with C' -> 'priority ranks every widening higher' (`Weighting.prior_lt_of_widens`); 'C alone gives no verdict' -> 'widening alone gives no verdict'. Open: 'Monotonicity at the standpoint (C placed at a standpoint; ...)' -> '**How an order holding one's own continuation forms** (self-concern, monotone at its standpoint): whether and how a life forms it, and how orders ranking by widening form where relations do not close'. Every theorem statement taking `Comparison` keeps 'C' (formal uses in §2, §4.4 routes, §5 Conditional (C) labels, the menu witness, second-order item). items.item: F3 what is joined, checked in the Lean and said exactly
items.how: Read MutualDependence.lean:138 (`Flow.MutuallyDependent.unrestricted`: Unrestricted (bounded fun q => L.WithinInfluence W (center q))), Feedback.lean (`WithinInfluence f g := WithinClosure (L.AffectedBy W) f g`; `AffectedBy g h := ∃ c, W.DependsOn g c ∧ L.Exchanges h c`; `Web.DependsOn g c := ∃ t, W.requires t g c`; `Exchanges` at some step), Retaining.lean (`bounded region p _ f := region p f`) and Weightings.lean:1503-1553 (`selfAscribed content center p t g := content (center p) t g`; `ownClosure rel c _ g := WithinClosure rel c g`): both unfold to WithinClosure AffectedBy (center p) g, so the step is proved, near-definitionally.
